site.name: privacy-dashboard
site.summary: privacy-dashboard-clone Generic / abstract privacy management panel (not tied to any specific brand). Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Single-page panel: top account banner, section cards (activity data / personalized ads / location / search / devices), each card with a toggle + "Details" link + "Delete my X data" button; prominent danger zones for Download my data and Delete account; privacy-policy links in the footer | | `styles.css` | Cards, toggle switches, warning colors (yellow / red), confirmation modal styles | | `script.js` | Toggle coordination, delete second-confirmation modal, form mock submission, status indicators |

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore the single-page privacy dashboard, validating the main privacy-management flow plus adjacent in-page navigation, recommendation shortcuts, destructive/recovery states, and responsive behavior.
run_plan.summary: The run should treat index.html as a rich single-page application with multiple sections and stateful controls rather than a multi-page site. Start by mapping the in-page navigation and recommendation shortcuts, then deeply exercise the privacy controls, activity management, export, and destructive actions, with special attention to dialogs, confirmations, and status changes driven by script.js. Repeat the most critical interactions on mobile because the prescan already shows multiple undersized tap targets in the top nav and left rail.
assumptions: Only index.html is a known HTML page; adjacent flows are likely in-page sections, dialogs, anchored panels, or dynamically revealed states rather than separate documents.
script.js likely coordinates toggle/state changes, delete confirmations, mock form submission, and status indicators, so visible UI changes after interaction are expected and should be verified.
The three detected dialogs are likely tied to confirmation/destructive workflows and deserve explicit coverage.
Header nav items, left-rail section buttons, and recommendation cards may scroll or switch the visible section within the same page instead of navigating away.
risk_hotspots: Delete-data actions across category cards: high-risk destructive flow with potential confirmation and unclear recovery
Download/Export data controls: important trust-sensitive flow that may use form submission or modal confirmation
Delete account / danger-zone controls mentioned in README: highest-risk irreversible action and confirmation UX
Toggle switches for activity/ad/location/search/device-related controls: verify state persistence within session, labels, and status summary updates
Dialogs/modals on index.html: confirm open/close behavior, focus trapping, dismiss paths, and secondary-confirmation wording
Privacy checkup panel and Start button: likely shortcut into a multi-step in-page flow with completion indicators
Recommendation cards (review activity saving, adjust ad personalization, inspect connected apps, create a data export): likely deep links into important sections
Left sidebar section buttons and top navigation tabs: likely duplicate navigation patterns that could become inconsistent
Mobile tap targets in header and sidebar: prescan already flags several below 44px height

phases.title: Map structure and navigation model
phases.objective: Confirm how the single page is organized and whether header nav, sidebar nav, and recommendation shortcuts reveal/scroll to distinct sections consistently.
key_checks: Use top header items (Privacy, Data controls, Apps, Devices) and verify whether they scroll, highlight, or change visible content without breaking context
Use left-rail buttons (Overview, Activity history, Data controls, Ad personalization, App access, Devices & locations, Export data, Settings) and verify each lands on a distinct section/state
Open the Privacy checkup Start path and compare it to the recommendation cards to see whether they target the same destinations
Check whether active/selected nav state updates correctly when moving among sections
Verify that section transitions preserve orientation and do not hide key summary cards or action buttons unexpectedly
exit_criteria: All visible navigation groups have been exercised at least once
The run has identified the major in-page sections and which controls are duplicate entry points
Any broken, no-op, or confusing navigation patterns are documented

phases.title: Exercise privacy controls and status indicators
phases.objective: Validate the core privacy-management flow by changing control states and checking whether summaries, indicators, and explanatory copy stay coherent.
key_checks: Find and toggle the visible privacy controls related to activity saving, ad personalization, location/search/device categories, and note any dependent or coordinated behavior
Verify whether the 'Controls active' summary updates when controls are changed
Inspect any auto-delete setting controls and test whether changing the retention selection updates visible status text
Use 'Details' or 'Manage' affordances in category cards such as Search history, Browsing history, Location history, and Voice activity to reveal more granular controls if available
Confirm status indicators, completion marks, or badges in the Privacy checkup/recommendations panel reflect updated control states
Check whether control labels clearly communicate on/off consequences before any destructive or privacy-reducing change is applied
exit_criteria: Most primary privacy toggles or control widgets visible in the page have been exercised
At least one summary metric or status indicator has been verified to react to control changes, or a lack of reaction has been noted
The relationship between detailed controls and dashboard summaries is understood

phases.title: Inspect activity history and category management
phases.objective: Validate how users review, drill into, and potentially remove sample activity across categories and time ranges.
key_checks: Use the activity-by-category time filters (30d, 90d, 1y if present) and verify chart/state changes are visible and understandable
Open Manage actions for Search history, Browsing history, Location history, and Voice activity to inspect deeper states or controls
Open Recent activity and any visible item-level actions such as Details to verify drill-in behavior
Test category-specific delete actions such as 'Delete my X data' if exposed, and confirm scope clarity before confirming
Observe whether counts like saved items or category item totals change after deletion or remain static as a mock; document the behavior either way
exit_criteria: All visible activity categories have been visited or invoked through their Manage/Details entry point
Time-range controls and at least one recent-activity drill-in have been exercised
At least one category-level deletion workflow has been explored up to and including confirmation/cancel paths

phases.title: Validate export and destructive confirmations
phases.objective: Stress the highest-risk flows involving data export, deletion, and account removal, with careful attention to safeguards and recovery paths.
key_checks: Use the prominent Export data button and the left-rail Export data section to compare entry points and verify any form or mock submission flow
If a dialog opens for export, validate required fields/options, submit behavior, completion/status messaging, and cancellation
Trigger delete-data actions from category sections and inspect first-confirm and second-confirm steps, wording clarity, and reversibility cues
Locate and exercise the danger-zone actions described in the README, especially Download my data and Delete account, without assuming external navigation
Verify all dialogs can be dismissed via explicit close/cancel, backdrop, and keyboard if supported
Check whether post-action success/error indicators appear and whether the page remains stable after destructive-flow cancellation
exit_criteria: Export flow has been exercised from at least one entry point through its terminal visible state
At least one destructive deletion flow and the account-deletion flow have been tested through both cancel and confirm branches if possible
Modal/confirmation usability issues, especially around irreversible actions, are documented

phases.title: Responsive and mobile validation
phases.objective: Repeat the most important navigation and high-risk interactions on mobile to assess reachability, tap accuracy, and dialog usability.
key_checks: Re-check header nav, search, help, account menu, and left-rail or collapsed navigation behavior on mobile viewport
Validate the already-flagged small tap targets in top navigation and section navigation for practical usability
Repeat one primary control-toggle flow, one recommendation shortcut flow, one export flow, and one destructive confirmation flow on mobile
Confirm dialogs fit the viewport, keep primary/secondary actions visible, and do not trap content off-screen
Check whether charts, cards, and summary metrics remain readable without horizontal clipping
exit_criteria: Critical desktop flows have been spot-checked on mobile
Known tap-target risks have been confirmed or disproven with interaction evidence
Any mobile-only layout, scrolling, or modal issues have been captured

coverage_targets.pages: Visit the only known HTML page (index.html) and traverse all major in-page sections, dialogs, and dynamically revealed states reachable from navigation, recommendation cards, manage/details links, export, and destructive actions.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise most visible controls on the key page: navigation groups, privacy checkup shortcuts, category Manage/Details affordances, time filters, primary toggles, export flow, and destructive confirmations including cancel and confirm branches where safe.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks on mobile viewport for navigation, undersized tap targets, one representative control-change flow, one recommendation shortcut, one export path, and at least one destructive confirmation/modal.

notes: Do not spend time searching for additional HTML pages unless interaction clearly opens them; prescan only shows index.html.
Because there are many controls (125 buttons, 34 inputs), prioritize user-critical and risk-heavy controls over exhaustive low-value button clicking.
Footer privacy-policy links exist per README and can be sanity-checked, but the main effort should remain on the dashboard's privacy-management workflows.
Capture whether visible counts and completion states are live-updating, mocked, or inconsistent after actions.

ux_notes: Tapping the device-level "Sign out" button on mobile opened a confirmation modal, so the action has a safeguard rather than signing out immediately.
The modal preserves device context by naming the specific device: visible text says "Sign out device?" and "Surface Laptop 6 will be signed out," which clarifies scope.
The destructive confirmation uses a primary red button labeled "Delete" instead of "Sign out," creating a wording mismatch for this device action.
The surrounding device card remains dimmed but visible behind the modal, helping maintain context for which device is being affected.

step.objective: Learn whether canceling the mobile device sign-out modal is easy, clearly reversible, and returns users to a stable device-management state without side effects.
step.success_criteria: The confirmation modal should dismiss, the Devices & locations page should remain intact, and no misleading sign-out/deletion success feedback should appear.

result.feedback: Visible content changed after the action.

result.feedback: Visible content changed after the action.

ux_notes: Clicking mobile Help did not open a panel, menu, dialog, or navigate away; the page stayed on the same URL and only showed a toast-style message: "Help opened for this demo dashboard.", which is weak support/recovery feedback for a privacy dashboard.
The Help control itself is a small mobile tap target (38x38px per layout warning), below 44px guidance, which may make support access harder on touch devices.
